newsitem.title: USA: Kmart doesn't see writedown from Canada deal.
newsitem.headline: Kmart doesn't see writedown from Canada deal.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Monday its sale of Kmart Canada Co to an investor group including York Management Services Inc would not result in further writedowns of the assets of the operation.

Earlier, Kmart said it sold 87.5 percent of Kmart Canada to York Management and two other investors. Kmart will retain the remaining 12.5 percent of the business and does not anticipate playing a management role in the operation.
"From our point of view, it's purely an equity interest, not a management interest," said Kmart spokesman Robert Burton.

In the fourth quarter, the discount store giant took a $98 million pre-tax charge to write down the value of its international operations. The retailer said Monday it believes it has fully written off the assets of Kmart Canada.
"We don't anticipate that there will be a need for further writedowns," Burton said. "We were somewhat in the ballpark with our initial expectations."
The sale was one of several steps the retailer has taken recently to shed international operations and focus on fixing its core U.S. store base.

In February, Kmart and its Mexican partner El Puerto de Liverpool SA de CV each agreed to sell their 50 percent interests in Kmart Mexico to Controladora Comercial Mexicana SA for a total of $148 million in cash.
